newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania's bourse not ready for privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania's bourse not ready for privatisation.

text.p: Lithuania's infant stock exchange is too weak now to handle the privatisation of large state companies, an official at the European affairs ministry said on Monday.
"We have to be frank, the market is too weak," Vytenis Junevichius, director of the privatisation department at the European affairs ministry, told Reuters.
The Euro ministry is overseeing the privatisation of 13 major state-owned enterprises that are to be sold by open, international tender, including Lithuanian Telecom.
The list originally included 14 companies, but the Baltic Shipyard has been excluded following a 43 percent buy-out by a Danish investor.
Junevichius said earlier attempts to sell small stakes in state companies on the stock exchange did not succeed.
"We have a problem selling small interests owned by the state in various companies," Junevichius said.

The investment community has had high hopes that the privatisation of large enterprises would inject much needed liquidity into the bourse, which has been struggling to regain the momentum it had in January when prices soared to record highs.
"I hope that privatisation will have a positive impact on the local capital markets, but I cannot say when it will happen ...next year, two years or in five years," Junevichius said.
"Right now they have a high supply of equity on the market, but they have no demand for equity," Junevichius added.
Officials have said they are mulling the idea of selling a stake of Lithuanian Telecom to a strategic investor and then selling shares on the market at an increased value.
Junevichius said this may be the pattern for the sale of other key state assets.
"We are not going to put these companies on the Lithuanian exchange right now," Junevichius said.
"First of all, it will be a private placement, with sales to strategic investors," he said.
"Having increased the value of the company, we can sell the remaining state interest on the local market or whatever market was wanted - Luxembourg, London, Stockholm or Helsinki," he said.
